candidates.assignee: Ascidian Therapeutics, Inc.; University of Pennsylvania
candidates.title: Trans-splicing molecules
candidates.relevance_note: CORE GENUS application. Claim 1 recites generic nucleic acid trans-splicing molecule (binding domain + splicing domain + coding/exon domain) in 3'-5' or 5'-3' orientation - the foundational 'exon editor molecule' architecture; spec covers ABCA4 and CEP290.

candidates.assignee: Ascidian Therapeutics, Inc.; University of Pennsylvania
candidates.title: Trans-splicing molecules
candidates.relevance_note: CORE granted patent of the genus family (priority 2018-04-17). Granted claim 1 recites nucleic acid trans-splicing molecule with binding domain narrowed to target ABCA4 introns (19/22/23/24) + splicing domain + coding domain. 3'-to-5' orientation.

candidates.assignee: Ascidian Therapeutics, Inc.; University of Pennsylvania
candidates.title: Trans-splicing molecules
candidates.relevance_note: CORE granted patent, sibling of US11993776 in same genus family. Claim 1: nucleic acid trans-splicing molecule, 5'-to-3' orientation (binding domain + splicing domain + exon coding domain).

candidates.assignee: Ascidian Therapeutics, Inc. (and University of Pennsylvania)
candidates.title: Trans-splicing molecules
candidates.relevance_note: Australian family member of the core 'Trans-splicing molecules' genus (priority 2018). Same exon-editor architecture.

candidates.title: ABCA4 trans-splicing molecules
candidates.relevance_note: Disease-specific (ABCA4 / Stargardt; underlies ACDN-01) trans-splicing exon-editor molecules. Inventors incl. Krumbach, Dooley, Doi, Gray, Bell. Claims narrowed to ABCA4 correction.

candidates.title: HTT trans-splicing molecules
candidates.relevance_note: Disease-specific exon editor for Huntington's disease (replaces mutant HTT exon 1 with normal CAG-repeat exon). Binding domain targets HTT intron 1. Inventors Doi, Gray, Peng.

candidates.title: Optimized acceptor splice site module for biological and biotechnological applications
candidates.relevance_note: Granted patent for ViGeneron REVeRT mRNA trans-splicing. Claim 1: pre-mRNA trans-splicing molecule with acceptor splice region (>=80% identity to SEQ ID NO:3). PCT/EP2019/086454; inventors Michalakis, Biel, Becirovic. Underpins VG801/dual-AAV ABCA4.

candidates.title: An optimized acceptor splice site module for biological and biotechnological applications
candidates.relevance_note: Published application of ViGeneron REVeRT family (parent of US12502438). Claim 1: pre-mRNA trans-splicing molecule with pyrimidine tract + NAGG acceptor splice site. PCT/EP2019/086454, priority EP 2018-12.

candidates.title: Split inteins and their uses
candidates.relevance_note: COMPARATOR. SpliceBio core PCT: engineered split inteins + degron to reconstitute large proteins (e.g. ABCA4) via dual-AAV PROTEIN trans-splicing. Mechanistically DISTINCT from RNA trans-splicing. Inventors Frutos, Caelles, Otero, Vila-Perello. Priority 2020-03-26.

candidates.title: Split inteins and their uses
candidates.relevance_note: COMPARATOR. EP member of SpliceBio split-intein/degron family (same as WO2021191447). Protein trans-splicing for large-gene reconstitution. NOT RNA trans-splicing.

candidates.title: Split inteins and their uses
candidates.relevance_note: COMPARATOR. US member of SpliceBio split-intein/degron family (WO2021191447 family). Protein splicing, mechanistically distinct from RNA trans-splicing.

candidates.assignee: Princeton University; Albert Einstein College of Medicine (Muir lab) - SpliceBio licensed foundation
candidates.title: Atypical split inteins and uses thereof
candidates.relevance_note: COMPARATOR / foundational academic intein patent (Muir lab) underlying SpliceBio's platform. Engineered fast/robust split inteins for protein trans-splicing. NOT RNA trans-splicing; assignee is academic, not SpliceBio.

candidates.title: Localization of trans-splicing nucleic acid molecules to and within the cellular nucleus
candidates.relevance_note: OUT-OF-TARGET company (Tacit, not Ascidian/ViGeneron/SpliceBio) but in-scope RNA trans-splicing exon-editor tech. Nuclear-localization domain to boost trans-splicing editing efficiency. Included for landscape context, low priority.

candidates.title: Methods and compositions for targeted trans-splicing
candidates.relevance_note: OUT-OF-TARGET company (Amber Bio, not a target) but in-scope RNA trans-splicing tech. Targeted pre-mRNA trans-splicing nucleic acid with binding/intronic domains + splice acceptor/donor + exon. Landscape context, low priority.
